sections.content:
You know verbs whose meaning shifts with indicative or subjunctive from C1 Unit 12 (*sentir que*, *decir que*, *decidir que*) and fronted objects picked up by a clitic pronoun from C1 Unit 11 (*ese argumento lo comparto*). Together, mood and word order let you say **exactly** what you mean without extra words.

Mood changes the speech act itself: *Siento que algo cambia* ('I sense that something is changing') vs *Siento que tengas que irte* ('I am sorry that you have to leave'); *Me dijo que venía* (report) vs *Me dijo que viniera* (instruction).

Fronting an object puts the known topic first and requires a matching clitic pronoun before the verb: *Esa frase la pulí ayer*, *A tus argumentos los respeto*. Leaving out the clitic (*Esa frase pulí ayer*) breaks natural Spanish syntax.

sections.title: Precision via mood & order
rows: *Siento que el tono mejora* ('sense') vs *Siento que no vengas* ('regret')
*Dijo que llega hoy* (fact) vs *Dijo que llegues hoy* (order)
*Ese matiz lo entiendo perfectamente.* (*lo* is mandatory)
*A ese público le interesa la claridad.* (*le* is mandatory)

items.spanish: Ese argumento incisivo lo comparto por completo, aunque moldearía el cierre.
items.english: That incisive argument I share completely, although I would shape the closing.

items.spanish: Siento que la frase gana fuerza cuando colocas el tema al principio.
items.english: I sense that the sentence gains strength when you put the topic at the start.

items.spanish: Siento que no hayas podido escuchar la charla completa.
items.english: I am sorry that you could not hear the whole talk.

items.spanish: El dominio del modo y del orden da a tu español una destreza muy expresiva.
items.english: Command of mood and word order gives your Spanish a very expressive skill.

sections.content: Whenever you front a definite direct object (*ese libro*, *esta idea*, *las notas*), always double it with *lo, la, los* or *las* before the verb (*esta idea la defiendo*, never *esta idea defiendo*). And check whether *sentir* or *decir* reports a fact/perception (indicative) or regret/an order (subjunctive).
